video.title: Companies Are Panic Paying for This Skill. Here’s How to Get In

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Brandon Gdosc, a Dallas-based former corporate 'AI operations' lead who five months earlier started a solo AI consulting and services business. He claims roughly $30k of small projects in the first six weeks, then growth to an ~$800k annual run rate (about $60-80k/month). He sells audits ($10-15k), fractional AI-executive retainers ($20-35k/month) and custom builds, mainly to 400-6,000 employee companies. Key takeaways: price high, ask discovery questions instead of solutioning, use a three-level solution framework, and build solutions yourself rather than just advising. The host promotes his own Playmakers community.

speakers.name: Brandon Gdosc
speakers.description: Founder of Gdosc Consulting, AI consultant in North Dallas, ex-financial adviser and corporate AI operations lead

ideas.name: Fractional AI consulting and implementation for mid/large companies
ideas.one_liner: Solo consultant with a small contractor team sells AI audits, fractional AI-executive retainers and custom-built AI/automation solutions to companies of hundreds to thousands of employees.
ideas.business_model: One-off audit fees, monthly fractional retainers, and project fees for built point solutions; follow-on work from discovered use cases.
ideas.customer: Mid-size (400-500 employee) and large (~6,000 employee) companies, plus some 40-50 person agencies and startups; executives under pressure to 'do something with AI'.
ideas.problem: Leadership has an AI mandate but no budget, no strategy, no in-house skills, and needs proof of ROI; employees have workflow pain points and unused ideas.
ideas.offer: AI readiness survey and report with chatbot, workshops, use-case discovery, a framework (AI operators, AI solutions briefs, three solution levels), a fractional AI executive role, and hands-on building of custom apps and agent automations.

pricing.model: Audit one-off fee; fractional monthly retainer; project-based builds; early hourly/retainer pricing
pricing.notes: He raised prices with each new deal, researching market rates via ChatGPT/Claude, which mostly surfaced big-consultancy rates. Point solutions after the audit are priced against a monthly spend budget.

acquisition_channels.details: Inbound interest from the start due to his reputation; referrals now exceed capacity; only one prospect got a sales follow-up.

quote.text: I have received more referrals uh than I've been able to service at this point
quote.speaker: Brandon Gdosc

acquisition_channels.details: Leveraged his existing network and reputation from prior AI operations work (e.g. a retainer from Rachel Woods as an early gig).
Executives ask him to talk with them as an 'AI expert'; discovery calls with warm contacts.

ideas.delivery: Brandon does discovery, then builds solutions himself with Claude Code (Next.js, MongoDB, Tailwind, Heroku) and no-code tools (Zapier, Relevance AI), with a developer and one other person helping. First 30 days often deliver 3-5 working solutions. He also runs workshops and acts as a fractional executive.
unit_economics_claims: About $30k of small projects in the first ~6 weeks
Grew to ~$800k annual run rate / roughly $60-80k a month by month 5
Team is himself, a developer, one other person, and tiny overhead
ideas.startup_cost: not stated (tiny overhead; computer and internet)
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Early projects within the first weeks/months; about $30k in the first six weeks

acquisition.how: Relies on reputation, referrals and personal calls; cold outreach to named execs is partly possible but trust-based sales need a human.

onboarding.how: The survey/readiness report and chatbot are automated, but discovery conversations and stakeholder alignment need a human.

delivery.how: Claude Code builds most apps, but a human must scope, supervise, handle security and change management, and be the trusted face.

billing.how: Invoicing and CRM are software; he built his own invoice tooling.

support.how: Clients want a personal relationship and handholding through adoption fear.

uk_applicability.notes: Demand for AI adoption is global. UK needs GDPR, data-protection and procurement awareness, and prices would likely be lower (GBP). Credibility and network are needed.

risks: Heavy dependence on founder's reputation and personal presence
Enterprise security, PII and procurement hurdles
Capacity limits: already turning away work

tactics.name: Ratchet pricing upward deal by deal
steps: Research market rates using ChatGPT/Claude, noting big-consultancy premiums
Price the first jobs low ($4-5k) for proof
Raise the price on each next proposal while you're confident of delivering value
Stop raising when value no longer justifies it

quote.text: I would do one at a at a certain price and the next one I would price a little bit.
quote.speaker: Brandon Gdosc

tactics.name: Discovery calls that ask, not solution
steps: Intro and rapport
Ask about their journey and feelings about AI
Ask about workflows and pain points ('where does that happen, how long')
Use SPIN-style implication questions
Do not offer solutions on the call
Return later with several engagement options

quote.text: I try to never solution on those calls.
quote.speaker: Brandon Gdosc

tactics.name: Three-level solution laddering
steps: Level 1: existing features in ChatGPT etc.
Level 2: stitch tools together (Zapier, Relevance AI)
Level 3: custom orchestrated builds mixing deterministic code and AI
Always start at level 1 and move up only if needed; level 2 often gives 80% of the benefit

tactics.name: Install internal AI operators
steps: Ask who in the client wants to work with you (5-10% are already keen)
Train them in discovery
Have them submit templated AI solutions briefs on a platform
Aggregate briefs for leadership to compute ROI and prioritise

tactics.name: Capture baseline time during discovery to prove ROI
steps: Ask how many hours each task takes
Log time saved per run on a dashboard
Point to savings later (e.g. 92 hours, $2,455)

tactics.name: Workflow-first mapping
steps: Use Miro or Lucid with the client
Map each box and what happens next
Find workflow opportunities before app ideas

warnings.warning: Companies with heavy PII (fintech, healthcare) are harder due to clearances and security.
Agentic AI promises are not yet fulfilled; be honest with clients about hype.
Staff may see consultant as threat to jobs; address fear and concerns.

lessons.lesson: A broad skill set plus AI leverage lets a technical generalist deliver work much faster; being able to build matters more than only advising.

quote.text: All my normal skill sets plus AI equaled like superpowers
quote.speaker: Brandon Gdosc

lessons.lesson: People tend to underprice; hot demand lets you ratchet price up until value is questionable.
Sell outcomes tied to revenue or cost savings; executives need proof AI isn't hype.
Consultants who build solutions, not just recommend, remove client friction and win more.
Start small projects, deliver, then expand; each project uncovers follow-on work.
Closing larger companies is not necessarily harder than small ones, but delivery involves more bureaucracy.
Credibility and honesty are a differentiator in a hype-filled market.
Hybrid deterministic code plus probabilistic AI is the most reliable agentic pattern right now.
Timing of a hot market plus matched skills makes the work hard but not complicated; reputation reduced the need to hustle for leads.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with specific price points and revenue trajectory, but only five months in, self-reported, unverified, lumpy revenue, a pre-existing network and background; the host's 'zero to $80k/month' framing is stronger than Brandon's own numbers (~$800k run rate).
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host sells the Playmakers AI community and reads a website.online sponsor ad.
